question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we decompose the exponent into a product of smaller exponents. For example,

$$
{12}^{4}=(3\cdot 4)^{4}={3}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2}\cdot {4}^{2}\cdot {4}^{2}.
$$

Next, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & ≡9\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡1\cdot 8+1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡1\cdot 0+1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡1\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\ {4}^{2} & ≡16\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡2\cdot 8+0\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡2\cdot 0+0\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡0\, & (\text{mod}\,0)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{12}^{4} & ≡{3}^{2}\cdot {3}^{2}\cdot {4}^{2}\cdot {4}^{2}\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡1\cdot 1\cdot 0\cdot 0\, & (\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡0\, & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{12}^{4}\text{ mod }8=0.
$$
